summary.title: Keras Tutorial: How to get started with Keras, Deep Learning, and Python
summary.one_liner: You learn to load your own image dataset from disk, train a simple neural network and a CNN (SmallVGGNet) with Keras, evaluate them, and run predictions on new images.
keywords: train neural network on custom dataset
how to make predictions with trained keras model
takeaways: How to organize an image dataset on disk into class folders and load it with imutils and OpenCV
How to one-hot encode labels with scikit-learn's LabelBinarizer and split data into training and testing sets
How to define, compile, and train a simple fully connected Keras network (3072-1024-512-3) using SGD and categorical cross-entropy
How to evaluate a model with a scikit-learn classification report and plot training/validation loss and accuracy
The tutorial also covers a SmallVGGNet CNN and a predict.py script to classify new images with a saved model
summary.summary: The tutorial teaches Keras basics by training models on a custom 3-class image dataset (cats, dogs, pandas) rather than built-in MNIST or CIFAR-10. It walks step by step through installing dependencies, loading and resizing images from disk, scaling pixels, creating train/test splits, one-hot encoding labels, defining a Sequential dense network, compiling with SGD, fitting, and evaluating with a classification report and loss/accuracy plots. The author notes the simple network reaches about 60% accuracy, and the page outlines a follow-up CNN (SmallVGGNet) and a prediction script. The page states it was updated to be TensorFlow 2+ compatible in 2020.
